key_insight: Power-law measurement spectra preserve a spurious-minimum-free landscape in low-rank matrix sensing, yet division-normalised optimizers can stall when weak-direction curvature falls below their effective denominator floor.
engineering_relevance: Optimizer denominator precision, not just problem conditioning, can limit convergence, with the predicted failure boundary depending on matrix size V and rank D.
method: Replace isotropic Gaussian measurement designs with covariance Σ = diag(j^−s).
Derive leading-order smallest non-gauge expected Hessian curvature scaling as V^−(s+1)D^−s.
Predict the critical exponent from the optimizer’s effective denominator floor and a calibrated detection lag.
evidence_signal: After calibrating Adam’s detection lag on four configurations and freezing it, the formula predicted onset within 0.45 in exponent s across all 16 held-out V × D grid cells and distinguished fixed-VD pairs.
watch_item: The approximation fails at D = 2 and saturates below ε₀ = 10^−8 at a dynamical floor, limiting extrapolation to very low rank or smaller denominator settings.
paper_title: The Precision Wall: An Optimizer-Dependent Boundary for Optimization under Power-Law Measurement Spectra
